{"filepath":"baseline_metrics.md","content":"Baseline metrics — Make it better
Date: 2026-09-06
Prepared by: Data & Systems Specialist
Source: research_findings.md (Alice) + required external analytics/data sources (see Access section)

Purpose
- Define measurable success metrics aligned to Alice’s research and the project goal “Make it better.”
- Locate or provide extraction methods for baseline data.
- Provide quick queries/commands and a baseline reporting template.
- If access is not available, list exact access steps required and provide realistic sample baselines for planning.

Summary / quick answer
- We do not have live analytics / DB credentials in this workspace. I list exact access steps and the SQL/API queries to run. I also include sample expected baselines (industry ranges) so the team can start planning and target-setting before we obtain data.

1) Metrics (definitions, measurement method, target)
- Front-end performance (Core Web Vitals)
  - Largest Contentful Paint (LCP): time (seconds) for largest above-the-fold element to render. Measurement: Real User Monitoring (RUM) 75th-percentile per device. Target: < 2.5s (Google CWV).
  - Interaction to Next Paint / INP (or FID historically): measurement: RUM median / 75th-percentile. Target: INP < 200 ms.
  - Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS): RUM 75th-percentile. Target: CLS < 0.1.
  - % pages meeting Core Web Vitals (per device): percent of page loads that meet all three targets. Target: > 90% (project target; adjust to feasibility).

- Acquisition & engagement
  - Sessions (users × sessions), by channel (organic, paid, direct, email). Measurement: GA4 (or UA) aggregated for 28d and 90d windows.
  - Bounce rate / Engaged sessions per user: GA4 engagement metrics. Target: improve by X% (set after baselining).

- Conversion & revenue
  - Site conversion rate (sessions → transaction): transactions / sessions (or users). Measurement: analytics / orders DB. Target: +10–20% uplift (as a project goal), subject to baseline.
  - Checkout conversion rate (checkout-start → transaction): measure funnel drop. Target: reduce checkout abandonment by 5–15 percentage points.
  - Cart abandonment rate: (added-to-cart events without purchase) / added-to-cart events. Industry baseline ~70% (Baymard). Project target: reduce by 5–10p.
  - Revenue per visitor (RPV) and average order value (AOV): revenue / sessions and revenue / orders.

- Reliability & backend performance
  - API latency (p95, p50) for core endpoints (product catalog, checkout). Measurement: application metrics (Prometheus/NewRelic/Sentry/AWS CloudWatch). Target: p95 < X ms (define after baseline; common target for critical APIs is <500 ms p95).
  - Error rate: 5xx errors / requests, and application exception rate. Target: <0.5% errors for user-critical endpoints.
  - Uptime: % available (SLA), measured via monitoring. Target: 99.9%+.

- Observability / tags / 3rd-party impact
  - Number of third‑party scripts loaded on key pages and their blocking impact. Measurement: synthesized audits (Lighthouse / WebPageTest) and tag manager listing. Target: reduce blocking 3rd-party scripts and lazy-load non-critical ones.

- Accessibility & SEO
  - WCAG 2.1 AA violations: number of critical violations per prioritized templates. Measurement: axe-core or pa11y automated scans + manual checks. Target: zero critical violations for priority flows.
  - Organic sessions & Core Web Vitals correlation: monitor organic traffic change after improvements.

2) Measurement windows and segmentation
- Windows: 7d (fast changes), 28d (monthly), 90d (seasonal), 12mo (historic trends).
- Segments: device (mobile/desktop/tablet), geography (top 5 countries), channel (organic/paid/direct/referral/email), new vs returning users, landing page types (category/product/checkout/home), browser major versions.

3) Data sources (typical) and what I need access to NOW
- Google Analytics 4 (GA4) property + BigQuery export (if available)
  - Need: GA4 property ID, ability to link / BigQuery dataset name or grant to service account.
- BigQuery dataset (GA4 export) or analytics warehouse (Snowflake/Redshift/BigQuery)
  - Need: project ID, dataset name, read-only service account with BigQuery Data Viewer.
- Server & CDN logs (CloudFront / Fastly / nginx) — for synthetic baseline and origin latency
  - Need: S3 bucket / log storage path or access to logs via logging console (CloudWatch / GCP logging) + credentials.
- Application DB / Orders data (Postgres / MySQL / Redshift)
  - Need: read-only credentials or a read-replica connection string, schema description (table names: orders, sessions, cart_events), and sample event/column names.
- Error & performance monitoring (Sentry, New Relic, Datadog, Prometheus)
  - Need: view access or API key to query error rates, latency histograms.
- Client-side RUM / web-vitals table (if implemented) — often exported to BigQuery or analytics warehouse
  - Need: dataset/table name and field mapping (e.g., lcp_value, inp_value, cls_value, page_url, device_category).
- Lighthouse / WebPageTest / PageSpeed Insights API
  - Need: API key for PageSpeed Insights (optional) or permission to run Lighthouse CI on CI/staging.

If any of the above are missing, the exact access steps are below.

4) Exact access steps (copy/paste friendly)
- Google Analytics 4 (UI)
  1) Open analytics.google.com and sign in with the project account.
  2) Provide me (or our service account) Viewer role on the GA4 property (Analytics Viewer) and link to BigQuery export if not already linked.
  3) If BigQuery export exists: give service account BigQuery Data Viewer on the analytics export dataset.

- BigQuery (if GA4 export exists)
  1) GCP Console → IAM & Admin → Add member: <service-account-email> role BigQuery Data Viewer.
  2) Share project ID and dataset name (e.g., my-project.analytics_123456.events_intraday_*) to allow query access.

- Snowflake / Redshift / Postgres
  1) Provide read-only user credentials (host, port, database, schema, username, password, whitelisting IP if needed), or grant SELECT on analytics schema to the service account.
  2) Provide minimal table descriptions: orders (order_id, user_id, created_at, total_amount, currency, status), sessions (session_id, user_id, started_at), cart_events (event_type, user_id, session_id, product_id, timestamp).

- CDN / server logs
  1) Share S3 bucket name and path or give me access to logging console (AWS Console > S3 or CloudFront) or GCP logging access.
  2) If using Cloudflare, add account/collaborator access to view analytics and raw logs export.

- Error/perf tools (Sentry / Datadog / NewRelic)
  1) Add a user with read-only role or create an API key with read permissions for the relevant project/app.

- Lighthouse / PageSpeed Insights
  1) Provide PageSpeed Insights API key (optional). Or grant repository/CI access to run Lighthouse CI against production/staging URLs.

5) Queries & commands to extract baselines (copy/paste ready)
Note: adapt table/field names to your schema. I provide GA4 BigQuery and generic Postgres examples.

A) GA4 export — sessions, transactions, revenue (BigQuery)
-- Replace `project.dataset.events_*` and event names/params per export schema
WITH events AS (
  SELECT
    event_date,
    event_name,
    (SELECT value.string_value FROM UNNEST(event_params) WHERE key='session_id') AS session_id,
    (SELECT value.int_value FROM UNNEST(event_params) WHERE key='ga_session_id') AS ga_session_id,
    (SELECT value.string_value FROM UNNEST(event_params) WHERE key='page_location') AS page_location,
    (SELECT value.double_value FROM UNNEST(event_params) WHERE key='value') AS revenue
  FROM
    `PROJECT.DATASET.events_*`
  WHERE
    _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20260101' AND '20260906' -- adjust date window
)
SELECT
  COUNT(DISTINCT session_id) AS sessions,
  COUNTIF(event_name='purchase') AS purchases,
  SUM(IF(event_name='purchase', revenue, 0)) AS revenue,
  SAFE_DIVIDE(COUNTIF(event_name='purchase'), COUNT(DISTINCT session_id)) AS conversion_rate
FROM events;

B) BigQuery — RUM web vitals 75th percentile (example table: web_vitals.events)
SELECT
  device_category,
  APPROX_QUANTILES(lcp_ms, 100)[OFFSET(75)]/1000 AS lcp_75s,
  APPROX_QUANTILES(inp_ms, 100)[OFFSET(75)] AS inp_75ms,
  APPROX_QUANTILES(cls, 100)[OFFSET(75)] AS cls_75
FROM `PROJECT.DATASET.web_vitals`
WHERE date BETWEEN DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 28 DAY) AND CURRENT_DATE()
GROUP BY device_category;

C) Postgres example — conversion and cart abandonment (generic)
-- Orders table: orders (id, user_id, status, amount, created_at)
-- Cart events table: cart_events (session_id, user_id, event_type, created_at)

-- Sessions, orders, revenue
SELECT
  COUNT(DISTINCT s.session_id) AS sessions,
  COUNT(DISTINCT o.id) AS orders,
  SUM(o.amount) AS revenue,
  (COUNT(DISTINCT o.id)::decimal / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT s.session_id),0)) AS conversion_rate
FROM sessions s
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.session_id = s.session_id AND o.status = 'completed'
WHERE s.started_at BETWEEN current_date - interval '28 days' AND current_date;

-- Cart abandonment
WITH carts AS (
  SELECT session_id,
         MAX(CASE WHEN event_type = 'add_to_cart' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS added,
         MAX(CASE WHEN event_type = 'purchase' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS purchased
  FROM cart_events
  WHERE created_at BETWEEN current_date - interval '28 days' AND current_date
  GROUP BY session_id
)
SELECT
  SUM(CASE WHEN added=1 AND purchased=0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS abandoned_carts,
  SUM(added) AS total_added,
  SAFE_DIVIDE(SUM(CASE WHEN added=1 AND purchased=0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), SUM(added)) AS cart_abandonment_rate
FROM carts;

D) WebPageTest / Lighthouse (synthetic)
- Lighthouse CLI (Node):
  npx lighthouse https://example.com --only-categories=performance --output=json --output-path=./lighthouse.json --emulated-form-factor=mobile
- PageSpeed Insights (curl)
  curl "https://www.googleapis.com/pagespeedonline/v5/runPagespeed?url=https://example.com&strategy=mobile&key=YOUR_API_KEY"

E) RUM-based percentiles using basic SQL (if web vitals stored as ms values)
SELECT
  page_path,
  COUNT(*) AS samples,
  APPROX_QUANTILES(lcp_ms, 100)[OFFSET(75)]/1000.0 AS lcp_75_seconds,
  APPROX_QUANTILES(inp_ms, 100)[OFFSET(75)] AS inp_75_ms
FROM `PROJECT.DATASET.rum_vitals`
WHERE date BETWEEN DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 28 DAY) AND CURRENT_DATE()
GROUP BY page_path
ORDER BY lcp_75_seconds DESC
LIMIT 50;

F) Sentry / errors (example API curl, substitute values)
curl "https://sentry.io/api/0/projects/{org_slug}/{project_slug}/issues/" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <SENTRY_API_TOKEN>" | jq '.'

6) Baseline report template (fields we will populate after queries)
- Window: (28d / 90d)
- Sessions (total, by device)
- Transactions / purchases
- Conversion rate (site-wide)
- Checkout conversion rate (checkout_start -> purchase)
- Cart abandonment rate
- Revenue, AOV, RPV
- LCP 75th-percentile (mobile / desktop)
- INP 75th-percentile (mobile / desktop)
- CLS 75th-percentile
- % pages meeting Core Web Vitals
- API p95 latency for checkout endpoints
- Error rate (5xx %)
- Accessibility: number of critical WCAG violations (per page/template)

7) Sample expected baselines (if we cannot access real data yet)
Notes: these are illustrative ranges (industry averages / research) for planning only.
- LCP (mobile) 75th-percentile: 2.5–6.0s (many sites average 2.5–4s). Target: <2.5s.
- INP (mobile) 75th-percentile: 100–600 ms.
- CLS 75th-percentile: 0.05–0.25.
- % pages meeting CWV: 20–70% depending on maturity.
- Sessions (sitewide): depends on business; use relative change targets.
- Conversion rate (ecommerce): 1–3% (retail average) — expected baseline 0.5–3%.
- Cart abandonment rate: ~60–75% (Baymard ~70%).
- Checkout abandonment: often 30–70% depending on flow complexity.
- Revenue per visitor: depends on AOV; use baseline from orders DB.
- Error rate (5xx): 0.1–1% typical; higher indicates issues.

8) Targets and prioritization guidance (quick wins vs bigger wins)
- Quick wins (1–3 days): image optimization, critical CSS, defer non‑critical 3rd‑party scripts, caching/CDN. Measurement: reduce LCP median/75th and improve % pages meeting CWV. Target: move mobile LCP 75th from e.g., 4s → 2.5s.
- Medium (1–4 sprints): checkout simplification, server-side rendering / edge rendering, consolidate tags. Measurement: improved checkout conversion, reduced cart abandonment. Target: increase checkout conversion by 5–15% relative.

9) Acceptance criteria (example)
- Performance: mobile LCP 75th <= 2.5s across 28-day window and % pages meeting CWV >= 90% for top 20 pages.
- Conversion: site conversion rate improvement >= +10% vs 28-day baseline, with p < 0.05 in A/B test (if used).
- Cart abandonment: reduction of at least 5 percentage points vs baseline across 28 days.

10) Next actions & checklist (what I need from you)
- Provide one or more of the following access items (preferred order):
  1) GA4 property ID + BigQuery dataset name OR a BigQuery read-only service account.
  2) Read-only DB credentials for orders/sessions/cart_events (or a data-dump CSVs if security prevents DB access).
  3) Access to RUM web vitals export or confirmation that web-vitals is collected to BigQuery/warehouse.
  4) Access to Sentry/NewRelic/Datadog for error and backend latency.
  5) Permission to run Lighthouse CI against staging/prod URLs (or PageSpeed API key).

- If you cannot grant these immediately, share recent CSV extracts for:
  - orders (last 90 days)
  - sessions (last 90 days)
  - cart_events (last 90 days)
  - web_vitals (last 28 days) with columns: timestamp, page_path, device_category, lcp_ms, inp_ms, cls

11) If you give me access I will deliver (within 48–72 hours)
- A filled baseline report (baseline_metrics_filled.md) with measured values for all metrics above (28d and 90d windows) and segment breakouts (mobile/desktop/top countries/top pages).
- A short prioritized backlog of 5–8 specific remediation items with estimated effort and expected impact.
- Suggested A/B test plan for checkout/performance changes where relevant.

Appendix A — quick sanity-check numbers (example output table format)
Window: 28 days
- Sessions: 123,456
- Revenue: $456,789
- Orders: 2,345
- Conversion rate: 1.90% (2345/123456)
- Cart abandonment rate: 68.2%
- LCP (mobile) 75th: 3.8s
- INP (mobile) 75th: 320ms
- CLS 75th: 0.12
- API checkout p95: 980 ms
- Error rate 5xx: 0.9%

These numbers above are illustrative — they show the report structure and the expected field types and units.

Appendix B — Recommended quick queries (condensed)
- GA4 -> BigQuery: events_* query for conversion and revenue (see section 5.A)
- RUM vitals: compute 75th percentiles per device and page (see section 5.B and 5.E)
- Orders/cart: compute cart abandonment and checkout funnel conversion (see section 5.C)
- Lighthouse: run npx lighthouse for the 20 top pages and compute median/75th for LCP and CLS.

Contact / handoff
- Reply to this ticket with the requested credentials or CSV exports. If you prefer, give me a read-only service account and the project/dataset names and I’ll run the queries and return baseline_metrics_filled.md.

-END-
"}
